Resolves #21238

A `TreeStore` that generates its records from a reactive config, as the big-data example stores do, now projects an expanded parent added while it processes its configs instead of throwing. `splice()` asked whether the parent is visible with `me.indexOf(parentNode) > -1`, which scans `_items`, still `null` then. It now asks the projection's key map, `me.map?.has(parentId)`. That is the question the removal path already asks: O(1) instead of a scan per added child, and false before a projection exists. A parent new in the same batch is projected with its children through `newRoots`, as before.

Evidence: L2 (unit: the real `TreeStore` constructed in the unit runtime, red on dev and green at head) → L2 required (a store projection defect; the ACs name no host or browser surface).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 an expanded and a collapsed parent added during construction project like the same records loaded through `data` | CI-covered: `unit/data/TreeStoreConstructionAdd.spec.mjs`, two construction cases and two `data` controls |
| AC-2 the expanded construction case is red on dev and green at head | outside CI: on dev `5576021ba7` it threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'indexOf')` from `TreeStore.splice` (1 failed, 3 passed); at `098b335ee4` 4/4 |
| AC-3 `unit/data/TreeStore*.spec.mjs` stay green | CI-covered: the unit job; locally `unit/data/` and `unit/grid/` 1068/1068 at head |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. While probing, a record whose id is `'root'` turned out to collide with `#childrenMap`'s top-level key: out of scope, noted in defect note `b0454c89`.

- Red on dev `5576021ba7`: "an expanded parent added during construction projects its rows" threw at `src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1234` in `Collection.indexOf`. The other three cases passed, so the controls separate the construction path from the data.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; the unit baseline ran (`unit/data/` and `unit/grid/` 1068/1068).

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: Active falsification of `TreeStore#splice` (`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1152-1245`) on `dev` (`node --input-type=module`) surfaced an adjacent pre-existing multi-level batch-ingestion bug outside `#21238`'s construction scope: when a store *already* holds a projected expanded node (`unit-1`, `me.map.has('unit-1') === true`) and a caller adds a two-level expanded subtree in one batch (`store.add([{id: 'dept-1', parentId: 'unit-1', isLeaf: false, collapsed: false}, {id: 'person-1', parentId: 'dept-1', isLeaf: true}])`), step `2a` runs `collectVisibleDescendants(dept-1, visibleToAdd)` mid-loop at `i = 0` before `person-1` enters `#childrenMap.get('dept-1')`, and at `i = 1` `me.map?.has('dept-1')` (like `me.indexOf(dept-1) > -1` before) is still `false` because `dept-1` sits in `visibleToAdd` pending `super.splice` — leaving `visible` at `['unit-1', 'dept-1']` and dropping `'person-1'` from the flat projection. Verified pre-existing on `dev` and independent of `#21238` (construction-time single-batch `add()` starts with an empty `me.map`, so roots defer `collectVisibleDescendants` to step `2b` after `#childrenMap` is complete); routed as a non-blocking `defect-note` on `AGENT:*` per `pr-review-guide.md §2.5`.

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: `Neo.data.Store#afterSetData` (`src/data/Store.mjs:416`) guards initial `data` ingestion behind `if (me.configsApplied)` (running after `Collection#construct` initializes `me.items = me.items || []`), whereas subclass reactive `afterSet*` hooks that call `this.add()` run inside `Base#processConfigs` while `me._items` is still `null`.
